Summer Riding by Region

Summer is prime touring season, but not all regions are equal. Some are too hot, some are too crowded, and some are just right. Here's your region-by-region guide to the best summer riding across Britain.

June: The Sweet Spot

  • Scottish Highlands (★★★★★): Longest days (18+ hours of light), warm temperatures, and before the worst of the midge season. June is arguably the best month for Highland touring.
  • North Wales (★★★★★): Warm mountain riding with long days. Before school holidays mean quieter roads.
  • Lake District (★★★★): Beautiful but starting to get busy. Midweek riding is best.
  • Southern England (★★★★): Warm and pleasant. Can be very hot in heatwaves — stay hydrated.

July: Peak Season Management

  • Scottish Islands (★★★★★): Skye, Mull, Arran, Outer Hebrides. The ferry crossing filters casual tourists. Best weather month for islands.
  • Northumberland (★★★★★): Warm, quiet, and spectacular. England's best-kept summer touring secret.
  • North Pennines (★★★★): One of England's emptiest areas even in July. Great riding through open moorland.
  • Lake District (★★★): Very busy. Avoid weekends. Ride early morning for the best experience.
  • Cornwall (★★★): Hot but extremely busy. Narrow lanes + holiday traffic = frustration.

August: Beat the Crowds

  • Scottish Borders (★★★★★): Almost everyone bypasses the Borders for the Highlands. Their loss. Beautiful, empty, excellent riding.
  • Mid-Wales (★★★★★): Between Snowdonia and the Brecon Beacons, mid-Wales is blissfully quiet with superb roads.
  • North York Moors (★★★★): Heather season begins mid-August. Purple moorland is stunning.
  • Channel Islands (★★★★): Warm, compact, and different. A unique summer tour option.
Summer touring success is about choosing the less obvious destination. While everyone heads for the same famous spots, equally beautiful but quieter regions await the rider willing to explore beyond the guidebook recommendations.

Summer Touring Essentials

Summer touring demands hydration discipline. Carry a refillable water bottle and drink at every stop. Dehydration causes fatigue, headaches, and poor concentration — all dangerous when riding in hot conditions. Sports drinks with electrolytes are even better than water for replacing what you lose through sweating.

Sun protection is essential for all-day summer riding. Apply high-SPF sunscreen to your neck, wrists, and any exposed skin. The wind over a motorcycle removes the sensation of heat, so you don't feel the burn until it's too late. Lip balm with SPF prevents cracked, sunburned lips.

Evening riding in summer is a pleasure — temperatures cool, traffic reduces, and the golden light transforms landscapes. Plan some of your most scenic sections for the last two hours before sunset for the best combination of conditions and atmosphere.
keyTakeaways: June is the sweet spot: 18-plus hours of daylight in the Highlands, warm temperatures, and before the worst midges.
July is peak season, so favour the Scottish islands, Northumberland, and the North Pennines to escape the crowds.
August rewards the less obvious: the Scottish Borders, mid-Wales, and North York Moors stay quiet and beautiful.
The Lake District and Cornwall are hot but heavily congested in July; ride early morning or avoid weekends.
Hydration and sun protection are essential, as wind removes the sensation of heat and hides developing sunburn.

faq.q: Why is June considered the best summer month?
faq.a: June delivers the longest days of the year, with 18-plus hours of usable light in the Highlands, warm temperatures, and timing before the worst of the Scottish midge season. Roads are also quieter than July and August because the school holidays have not yet begun, making it the sweet spot for ambitious tours.

faq.q: How do I avoid crowds in peak season?
faq.a: Choose the less obvious destination. In July, the Scottish islands, Northumberland, and the North Pennines stay quiet while the Lake District and Cornwall are packed. In August, the Scottish Borders and mid-Wales are almost empty because everyone bypasses them for the Highlands. Ride early morning and midweek wherever possible.

faq.q: How do I manage heat on a summer tour?
faq.a: Carry a refillable water bottle and drink at every stop, as dehydration causes fatigue and poor concentration. Sports drinks with electrolytes are even better in the heat. Apply high-SPF sunscreen to neck, wrists, and exposed skin, because the wind removes the sensation of heat and you will not feel the burn until you stop.

faq.q: When is the best time of day to ride in summer?
faq.a: Early mornings and the last two hours before sunset. Evenings bring cooler temperatures, reduced traffic, and golden light that transforms landscapes. Plan your most scenic sections for late in the day, and hit popular roads before 9am when even the busiest tourist routes are still quiet.
